Yes, I could read it. Here is what happened.

## The release worked. The Homebrew step did not.

`v0.1.1` is published with all four archives plus `checksums.txt`. The job failed on the very last action:

```
homebrew formula: could not update "Formula/waythrough.rb":
PUT .../contents/Formula/waythrough.rb: 409 Could not create file:
Changes must be made through a pull request.
```

GoReleaser tried to commit `Formula/waythrough.rb` directly to `main`, and `main` has branch protection requiring a pull request with 1 code-owner approval. The `GITHUB_TOKEN` of `github-actions[bot]` is not an admin, so it has no bypass.

## The smallest fix

Branch protection on this repo has `enforce_admins: false`, and you have `admin: true` on it. So a PAT belonging to you **does** bypass the PR requirement, while the Actions bot token does not.

That makes the fix two lines: keep `.goreleaser.yaml` exactly as it is, and in `.github/workflows/release.yml` swap

```yaml
GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

for a PAT stored as a secret (Contents: read+write on this repo). No second repo, no extra workflow permission, no manual approval per release. The repo is public, but tag-push workflows do not expose secrets to forks, so that is fine — still, putting a PAT in a release workflow is your call, not mine.

The conventional alternative is a separate `gustavofsantos/homebrew-tap` repo. Also zero manual steps per release, but it needs a new repo, still needs a PAT (the Actions token is scoped to one repo), and changes the tap name in your README. The third option — `brews[].pull_request.enabled: true` — works but costs you an approve-and-merge on every single release, plus `pull-requests: write` in the workflow.

## Two things to know either way

**`brew install waythrough` is currently false.** There is no `Formula/` directory in `main` at all, and a tap only carries the latest formula. Fixing the config makes brew work from the *next* tag onward; `v0.1.1` gets a formula only if you open that PR by hand. Your choice which.

**Do not re-run the job.** The release is complete — re-running would re-run `scripts/check.sh` and rebuild all four targets for nothing, and it risks tangling with the already-published assets.

Separately, the log carries a `brews is DEPRECATED` warning. Do not treat that as a rename to fold into this fix: `homebrew_casks` is macOS-only, so migrating would drop the Linux brew support your current formula gives you. Worth deciding on its own.

Want me to apply the PAT change to the workflow, or set up the separate tap repo instead?

## What I actually changed — not quite what I proposed

I said "swap `GITHUB_TOKEN` for a PAT." I shipped something narrower: the release keeps the ephemeral bot token, and **only** the formula push uses the PAT, via `brews[].repository.token`. Publishing a release crosses no protected branch, so it needs no bypass. The practical difference is that the PAT needs `contents:write` on one repo rather than being the credential for the whole release run.

```
.goreleaser.yaml       brews[].repository.token: "{{ .Env.HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
release.yml            HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

## The secret you need to create

Make it a **classic** PAT with `repo` scope, not a fine-grained one. Admin bypass over classic branch protection is well-trodden for classic tokens; fine-grained token behavior against classic protection is the part I would not bet a release on, and if it fails it fails identically to today.

fix(release): commit the Homebrew formula with an admin token

Branch protection on `main` requires a pull request, and the ephemeral
Actions token acts as github-actions[bot], which holds no admin bypass.
The v0.1.1 release therefore published its archives and then failed with
a 409 when GoReleaser tried to commit Formula/waythrough.rb.

Give the `brews` block its own token, so that the formula commit uses a
credential owned by a repository admin, which the protection exempts.
The release itself keeps the ephemeral token, because publishing a
release crosses no protected branch.

An admin credential was confirmed to bypass the protection by replaying
the failed API call by hand. The remaining untested link is whether
GoReleaser honours `repository.token` for this push. If it does not, the
next tag fails with the same 409 on Formula/waythrough.rb.

A missing HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN secret fails late, after the release
is already published, so set the secret before the next tag.
